proposals.evidence: DEDR1619 gives Tamil/Malayalam kīḻ below, Kannada kīḻa/keḷagu, Kodagu kïḷï/kïda, Parji kiṛi and Kurux kiyyā beneath. Selected southern kiḷ-/kiś-/kɨg-/kɨh- survey variants and Parji/Gadaba kīḍi(n) are comparative extensions of that lower/below stem; Gadaba is supported comparatively by neighbouring Parji, not directly named in the article. Kurux kiya/kiye retain source final vowels; longer uncertain formations are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5475 explicitly gives Tamil veṭiyal/viṭiyal break of day or dawn, from veṭi/viṭi to dawn. These southern survey vɛḍiyalɛ/vɛḍiyala/bɛḍiyalɛ morning responses preserve the nominal dawn formation, including initial v/b and final vowel variants; they are comparative minority-lect extensions. Questioned Kota/Toda comparisons in the article are not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1769 gives Tamil kuraṅku, Malayalam kuraṅṅu, Kannada koraṅgi and Tulu kuraṅga monkey, with Kota korg/Toda kwarg. The selected southern survey koraŋg-/kuraŋg-/koraŋŋ- forms preserve that nasal-stop family, including Malayalam-type assimilation and final-vowel notation. The article’s explicit Tamil kōnti loan from Telugu is not used for these forms. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3656 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kota nāḷ day and Kannada nāḷ day/time. Selected southern survey nāḷ/naḷɨ/ṇāḷɨ retain this day stem; Mannan na is the proposed final-lateral-loss counterpart, qualified as a comparative lect extension. Longer temporal phrases are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
